topic: District-closed Layer-3 counterfactual transport from heterogeneous typed menus. For finite acyclic SCMs, require each selection domain to alter whole bidirected districts, define a source-labelled graphical recursion for observational, interventional, and declared partial-copy counterfactual inputs, and prove soundness plus fixed-declared-cardinality completeness: every failure produces two SCMs on the original state spaces with identical supplied laws but unequal target conditional counterfactuals. Return either an allowed rational identifying functional or an explicit paired-model certificate, with zero-denominator rejection. Apply it to Park-Lee transport and counterfactual-bandit arm pruning. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: On a fixed district response set, every supplied typed-menu cell is a zero-one incidence row applied to the district response-law vector. Stacking extractable rows gives a matrix A: a target row outside the affine row span admits an exact nullspace perturbation producing two same-cardinality laws with equal menus and unequal targets, while a row inside the span gives an affine identifying functional. District closure lifts the paired law across domains without partial-district leakage. The three-node transport witness checks target joint 1/4, target conditional 6/11, and source joint 3/8; the binary bow pair has identical observational laws but target values 1 and 1/2. Searches found existing CTFTR only for Layer-1/2 inputs and CTFIDU+ only for one-domain Layer-3 inputs. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that the source-labelled graphical recursion preserves all cross-menu information and fails exactly when the target district incidence row leaves the stacked affine span for every finite multi-district compatibility fiber. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate the smallest binary two-hedge thicket, form the exact rational incidence matrix of every supplied menu cell, and compare graphical failure with affine-span membership; any failed recursion whose target row lies in the span refutes the fixed-cardinality converse and should stop or pivot the run.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize identification of target-domain conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous source-labelled observational, interventional, and declared Layer-3 partial-copy menus under district-closed mechanism shifts by a terminating graphical recursion.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature resolves the two axes separately: CTFTR and mz-transportability retain domain labels but consume Layer-1/2 laws, whereas CTFIDU+ consumes Layer-3 laws without heterogeneous source labels. The prior monotone-counterfactual run also delivered only a global response-profile/CAD oracle and explicitly left graphical compression open. A source-labelled district recursion could discard linear constraints shared across menus, so the first missing proof step is an invariant that every recursive reduction preserves the joint row information induced by all source-labelled cells, followed by a district-invariance and local-to-global gluing argument for success and failure traces.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating source-labelled graphical algorithm with soundness and iff completeness theorems that returns an allowed rational functional for each positive-denominator target conditional and otherwise compiles its failure trace into two original-state-space finite SCMs agreeing on every supplied menu law.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from cross-environment heterogeneity to a formal counterfactual transport task and then to a complete graphical procedure.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Experiments and mechanisms differ across environments -> existing transport theory fuses observational and interventional laws -> decision-relevant counterfactuals must also move across domains -> heterogeneous Layer-3 menus require a source-labelled complete recursion

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the CTFIDU+ ctf-factor decomposition, IDENTIFY+ recursion, and ctf-hedge completeness proof while indexing every available factor and compatibility constraint by source domain.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves arbitrary-Layer-3 identification before the additional selection-diagram and cross-domain compatibility constraints are imposed.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over multiple-selection-diagram recursion and its completeness reduction for fusing information unavailable from any one source.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the multi-environment source-labelling half of the desired theorem, but only for Layer-2 effects.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile a successful rational functional into a multi-source one-step estimator using tangent-space decomposition, then prove asymptotic linearity under independent sampling and denominator separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The returned functional aligns components of several source laws, matching the multi-source data-fusion efficiency problem.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether failure of the source-labelled Layer-3 recursion is equivalent, on every fixed finite multi-district compatibility fiber, to the target incidence row lying outside the affine span of all supplied typed-menu rows.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hedgelet, thicket, and ctf-hedge proofs construct countermodels tailored to graphical obstructions, but do not equate recursion failure with the total affine information in a heterogeneous Layer-3 menu while holding every observed alphabet fixed. The banked nullspace proposal failed because a signed direction in the ambient response-law simplex need not lie in the latent-DAG or district-factorized realizability fiber. The first missing step is therefore a kernel or tangent characterization inside the exact finite multi-district compatibility fiber, plus a gluing theorem that turns a feasible direction into two positive same-cardinality SCM laws without changing any source menu cell; the smallest two-hedge thicket is the decisive early counterexample test.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an affine-span iff theorem converting each failed recursion into a nonzero feasible fiber direction and an explicit same-cardinality paired-SCM certificate, or a smallest rational two-hedge counterexample where recursion fails although the target row is in span.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames completeness around a concrete counterfactual hedge and makes constructive countermodel production central to the result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Layer-3 data enlarge identification -> completeness requires a failure witness -> ctf-hedges yield bit-encoded paired SCMs -> heterogeneous menus require an exact fixed-cardinality affine certificate or a refuting counterexample

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt hedgelet/thicket extraction and the recursive proof that each algorithmic failure exposes a graphical obstruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Thickets are the closest completeness witnesses for arbitrary collections of supplied laws, but those laws are Layer-2 rather than source-labelled Layer-3 cells.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the finite canonical response-function carrier to express every supplied and target cell as exact constraints before computing affine spans and feasible null directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed incidence matrix requires precisely the finite canonical representation established for discrete counterfactual laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Compile each successful rational graphical functional into an influence-function estimator and prove asymptotic normality under positivity and denominator separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An in-span target becomes a finite observed-law functional, so graphical-functional influence-function compilation is the natural inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the weakest within-district mechanism-change condition that permits sound transport of Layer-3 menus when selection alters only part of a bidirected district, or exhibit a minimal partial-district leakage witness.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Node-level selection diagrams and district/ctf-factor decompositions coexist in current transport theory, but the located literature gives no explicit invariance frontier for supplied Layer-3 menus when only some mechanisms inside a confounded district change. The first proof step that fails is the domain-invariance lemma for a transported ctf-factor: a source partial-copy law can constrain a cross-world coupling that has no target counterpart after one endpoint or its latent response kernel changes. Whole-district closure prevents this leakage, but it remains unresolved whether closure is necessary or a weaker separability condition suffices.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient condition on within-district selection and latent-kernel invariance licensing Layer-3 menu transport, with an identifying reduction under the condition and a smallest finite paired-SCM leakage certificate when it fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its selection-diagram motivation and ctf-factor formulation provide the closest language for explaining cross-domain leakage through confounded components.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Domains differ in selected mechanisms -> counterfactual queries couple multiple worlds -> ctf-factors localize shared latent structure -> partial-district changes require a precise invariance frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sC-component decomposition and s-hedge countermodels while tracking whether latent response kernels remain invariant for a whole district or only selected vertices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational complete analysis of how selection nodes interact with confounded components in transportability.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over ctf-factor consistency and ctf-hedge encodings to construct or rule out cross-world leakage under candidate partial-district invariance conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This machinery explicitly represents the cross-world response coupling that a partial district shift can corrupt.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive sharp target-domain bounds for conditional counterfactuals from heterogeneous Layer-3 menus when point transport fails, separating uniformly positive conditioning fibers from sometimes-positive and always-zero fibers.

source_refs.claim: Canonical finite SCMs reduce sharp counterfactual bounds from arbitrary observational and experimental inputs to polynomial programming.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Realizable Layer-3 data can tighten bounds for nonidentified counterfactuals, but the analysis does not supply heterogeneous-domain transport bounds.
source_refs.author: Arvind Raghavan, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: CTFTR gives a complete point-transport criterion for conditional counterfactuals but returns nontransportability rather than a sharp transported identified set.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: Partial-counterfactual programs treat one SCM with observational/interventional inputs, and current Layer-3 bounds do not add heterogeneous selection domains; CTFTR instead stops at point-transport failure. Combining them is not mechanical because district invariance couples response-law simplices across domains, typed menus impose shared equalities, and a conditional target is a ratio whose denominator can vanish on part of the compatibility fiber. Sharpness must therefore optimize over a multi-domain fiber and separately determine whether the conditioning event is uniformly positive, sometimes positive, or impossible.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite polynomial or linear-fractional program whose attainable extrema equal the sharp transported conditional-counterfactual bounds, together with extremizing SCM witnesses and a three-way denominator classification.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames bounds as the principled output after exact counterfactual identification fails and formulates them over finite canonical SCMs.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many counterfactuals are not point identified -> discrete SCMs admit finite canonical representations -> optimization yields sharp compatible ranges -> heterogeneous Layer-3 transport needs the analogous conditional multi-domain range

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt causal-constraint polynomialization, branch-and-bound, dual relaxations, and epsilon-sharp outer certificates to the multi-domain response-law fiber.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A transported conditional is a rational functional over constrained finite response laws, structurally matching Autobounds' polynomial causal programs.

method_exemplars.technique: Use canonical finite response functions and their proof of sharp finite reduction, augmented by shared district-kernel variables across source domains.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact finite carrier on which transported Layer-3 menu equalities and target extrema can be posed.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate bound endpoints from menu-cell frequencies and adapt confidence intervals that remain valid as the identified interval approaches a point.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The output is a causally identified interval whose width may shrink to zero, so sampling uncertainty must cover both partial- and point-identification regimes.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine when transported Layer-3 menu laws safely prune counterfactual structural-causal-bandit arms without removing a target-optimal arm, and quantify the regret gain from heterogeneous source information.

source_refs.claim: CTF-SCB admits realizable Layer-3 arms and graphically prunes the counterfactual action space, but does not transport heterogeneous source-domain data.
source_refs.author: Min Woo Park, Sanghack Lee

source_refs.claim: Transportable structural causal bandits fuse heterogeneous observational and experimental sources and obtain source-informativeness-dependent sublinear regret, but use Layer-1/2 inputs.
source_refs.author: Min Woo Park, Sanghack Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: The two Park-Lee papers cover complementary halves: one defines and prunes realizable counterfactual arms, while the other transports heterogeneous observational/interventional priors to accelerate a target bandit. Neither gives an arm-equivalence or domination criterion when source information itself contains Layer-3 menus. The first proof step that changes is the possibly-optimal-arm comparison because a target arm mean can now be rationally identified, only bounded, or undefined when a conditioning cell has zero mass; this status must be propagated without unsafe pruning before the online regret decomposition can use source precision.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graphical-algebraic safe-pruning characterization for transported Layer-3 arms, plus an online policy with a target regret bound depending explicitly on source-identified arm means, bound-separated arms, and rejected zero-denominator arms.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup connects heterogeneous offline causal information, target deployment, safe action-space reduction, and source-informativeness regret gains.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal structure avoids needless exploration -> heterogeneous source datasets contain reusable reward information -> transportability turns those sources into target priors -> Layer-3 menus should safely prune counterfactual arms

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt CTF-MIS/CTF-POMIS arm equivalence, counterfactual regime graphs, and the proof that representative pruning preserves an optimal realizable counterfactual arm.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the exact Layer-3 arm space and graph-theoretic pruning machinery needed at the destination.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt transported reward estimators and the bandit regret decomposition whose improvement is controlled by the informativeness of source priors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the desired sequential-learning consequence under heterogeneous sources before Layer-3 menus and conditional counterfactual rewards are introduced.

method_exemplars.technique: Use complete realizability testing and counterfactual-randomization semantics to certify that each retained Layer-3 arm corresponds to an executable sampling regime.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Safe pruning is operational only after formal counterfactual regimes are separated from physically realizable arms.

literature_map:
Shpitser and Pearl (2008, JMLR) give complete ID*/IDC* procedures for marginal and conditional counterfactuals from lower causal-hierarchy layers, including undefined conditioning evidence.
Bareinboim and Pearl (2012, AAAI) establish complete transportability through selection diagrams and s-hedges.
Bareinboim, Lee, Honavar, and Pearl (2013, NeurIPS) introduce multi-environment transport with limited experimental menus.
Bareinboim and Pearl (2014, NeurIPS) prove completeness for mz-transportability across multiple heterogeneous environments.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (2020, UAI) solve gID for arbitrary observational/interventional collections using hedgelets and thickets.
Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021, NeurIPS; arXiv:2107.03190) prove CUT and complete nested/conditional counterfactual identification from arbitrary surrogate experiments.
Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML) give CTFTR, complete counterfactual transport across domains from Layer-1/2 supplied laws.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML; arXiv:2110.05690) reduce partial counterfactual identification in finite discrete SCMs to canonical-model polynomial optimization.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) automate sharp discrete causal bounds via polynomial programming and certified relaxations.
Li and Luedtke (2023, Biometrika; arXiv:2111.14945) derive efficiency bounds and efficient one-step estimators for aligned multi-source data fusion.
Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025, ICLR; arXiv:2503.11870) characterize physically realizable Layer-3 distributions and counterfactual randomization.
Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026; arXiv:2602.23541) introduce CTFIDU+ for arbitrary Layer-3 inputs, ctf-hedge completeness, and Layer-3-assisted bounds, but not heterogeneous-domain transport.
Park and Lee (2026, ICLR) introduce realizable Layer-3 structural-causal-bandit arms and counterfactual action pruning.
Park and Lee (2026, UAI; arXiv:2511.17953) transport heterogeneous Layer-1/2 source information into structural causal bandits with source-informativeness-dependent regret.
The live boundary is the unoccupied intersection: source-labelled Layer-3 menu transport, its fixed-cardinality constructive converse, sharp failure bounds, and its safe bandit-pruning consequence.
